log.summary: The first staging test build of the vault, used to stand up the staging channel.
changes: First test build of the vault on the staging channel: enroll, unlock, lock and recovery inside a Nitro Enclave, with each vault sealed to this release's own key.
Built from vettid-vault commit 87187e7 (tag release/staging/1) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-04 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Test build adding connection requests with a short code that both people compare.
changes: Connection requests, with a short code that both people compare before they connect (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.10.2 and 0.10.3).
The release number and the release automation signing key are built into the image.
Built from vettid-vault commit bf0cc31 (tag release/staging/2) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-05 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Test build with notices for declined connections and pairings, recovery fixes and a capacity self-test.
changes: A declined connection request or a rejected device pairing is reported to the other side (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.10.5).
Recovery records when it was registered, and the vault keeps the credential backup setting (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.10.6).
Fixes from the first staging tests (queue recreation, lock logging, recovery test vectors) and a capacity measurement in the self-test.
Built from vettid-vault commit 5cd11db (tag release/staging/3), the first release built on the ubuntu-26.04-arm runners, and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-05 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Test build adding the daily owner check, enrollment codes, delegation statements and stricter credential and recovery rules.
changes: The daily owner check: a vault whose owner has not confirmed with PIN and password for 24 hours is held, and its agents pause, until the owner does (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.13.0).
Enrollment codes, app keys and account status (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.15.0).
Delegation and status statements in the LEASH format (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.12.0).
A credential can no longer be deleted on its own, and recovery needs the credential backup to be on (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.15.2 and 0.16.0).
A transferred app learns its account from the pairing, and errors say how long to wait before retrying (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.17.0).
Built from vettid-vault commit f5cf127 (tag release/staging/4) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-07 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Test build with your name always shared with connections, your full email in the account view, history search and item limits.
changes: Your shared profile always carries your first and last name, and you can change your name from the app (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.18.0).
The account view shows your full email, and your history can be searched inside the vault (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.20.0).
Kept values, item size limits, dry runs, named limits and fixes to sharing (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.21.0).
Built from vettid-vault commit 26b7140 (tag release/staging/5) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-08 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Test build adding History export and one template item per contact point.
changes: You can export your History from the vault (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.22.0).
Contact templates keep one item per contact point, without reserved tags (template registry version 2).
Built from vettid-vault commit 403d7d9 (tag release/staging/6) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-09 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Test build adding asks from connections, with rate limits per connection rule.
changes: Connections can ask you for information under rules you set, with rate limits per connection rule (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.23.0).
Fixes to merging tags and resuming asks (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.23.1).
Built from vettid-vault commit c22a750 (tag release/staging/7) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-09 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Test build that records which device unlocked or locked your vault in its history.
changes: Your vault's history records which device unlocked or locked it (VAULT-MESSAGING 0.23.2).
The build's base images come from the AWS ECR Public mirror at the same pinned digests; nothing else in the vault changes.
Built from vettid-vault commit 6a752d2 (tag release/staging/8) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-10 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Release 9 fixes a problem where your vault could lock itself again right after an update, and prepares it for push notifications through Google and Apple.
changes: Fixed: after updating, the vault could lock again within a minute and ask you to unlock once more. Unlocking a vault that is already open now keeps it open.
New: your vault can register this phone for push notifications, so that in a later app update notifications can arrive without the app's on-phone service.
The push carries no content: Google or Apple only learn that VettID woke your phone, never what for. Nothing changes until you choose Google push in the app.
Your vault's network access gains one address: VettID's push service for this channel (push.staging.vettid.org). Nothing else is added.

log.summary: Release 10 tightens how your vault checks your phone's app and records which version of VettID it was set up with.
changes: Security fix: the check that an app runs on a genuine, locked phone was tightened. Before, a specially built certificate chain could pass it. Your PIN and credential password were never bypassed by this.

New: your vault records which version of VettID it was set up with, signed by VettID or by Google, and shows it under Settings, Vault status. Changing version needs a transfer or a recovery with your PIN and password.
This test channel now has its own app, VettID Staging, which installs beside the production app. Each staging vault is attached to the new app once: by transfer, by recovery or by enrolling again.
Features your app does not use yet can now be left out of a release. On this channel all of them stay on, so nothing changes.
log.security_text: The vault accepted a phone's hardware attestation without checking that only the phone's own certificate carried the app's details. Someone with a real Android phone could have attached a modified app to a vault they could already enroll, receive by an approved transfer or recover. It did not bypass the PIN, the credential password, a transfer's approval or the recovery code. Release 10 refuses such certificate chains.

log.summary: Release 11 locks your vault when its host goes silent and tightens what a vault's process may do inside the enclave.
changes: If the host your vault runs on stops answering for two minutes, your vault now locks itself. Unlock it again with your PIN; nothing is lost.

Hardening: the process that runs your vault inside the enclave is refused more of the system functions it never needs, and can no longer create a private system environment of its own. Every release is tested for this on real hardware before it is offered.
The enclave is built with a newer version of its programming language, which includes fixes to the network and encryption code it uses.
Fix: a vault whose stored state had grown very large could be saved but not read back. The host now reads everything it can write.
Fewer and steadier connections between vaults and the relay. Nothing changes in how your messages are delivered.
log.security_text: Release 11 closes ways in which a fault in one vault's process could have reached beyond that vault inside the enclave, and updates the enclave's network and encryption code to a version with security fixes. We know of no use of either against any vault. Your PIN and credential password were not exposed.

log.summary: Release 12 fixes an unlock that could fail when several vaults unlocked at once, keeps vaults further apart, and lets only your phone approve connections.
changes: Fix: when several vaults on the same host unlocked at the same moment, an unlock could fail, and trying again worked. This was in every earlier staging release. Unlocks no longer fail this way.

Hardening: each vault process on a host now runs under an identity that is never given to another vault, anything a vault's process leaves running is stopped when it ends, and a vault's process can no longer write files.
Hardening: a vault's process can reach the record that names your vault, and your previous vault when you enroll again, only as far as enrolling and erasing need.

Only your phone can now approve a connection request, create or accept an invitation, start or accept an introduction, or approve a connection's request. A desktop can still decline or deny them; its older pending ones are refused.

Push registration now checks that a push token really belongs to the phone registering it: VettID's push service sends the phone a code and your vault confirms it. Nothing changes for you until push notifications arrive in a later app update.
log.security_text: Release 12 closes ways in which a fault in one vault's process could have reached another vault's process on the same host: an identity could be given again to the next vault, and something a process left running could have outlived it. It also narrows what a vault's process may write to the record that names a member's vault. We know of no use of any of these against any vault. Your PIN and credential password were not exposed.

log.summary: Release 13 runs your vault on a newer, hardened kernel, lets its process use only the system calls it needs, and fixes long conversations that would not open.
changes: Fix: opening a long conversation could fail with no answer, and trying again failed the same way. Messages now come in pages, newest first, and a reply too large to send is answered with an error instead of silence.

Hardening: the enclave now runs Linux 6.6.158, built by VettID from kernel.org source with a hardened configuration and reproduced on two builders, instead of the older kernel supplied with AWS's tools. Every release carries a copy of it and its source.
Hardening: the kernel now refuses module loading, kernel replacement, user namespaces and other features a vault does not use, and the vault does not start unless these settings hold.
Hardening: a vault's process may now make only the system calls it is known to need, may not start other programs, and cannot see other vaults' processes.
log.security_text: Release 13 narrows what a fault in a vault's process could reach: the enclave's kernel is current and hardened, and a vault's process can use only the parts of it the vault needs. Earlier releases ran an older kernel and refused only a short list of system calls. We know of no use of this against any vault. Your PIN and credential password were not exposed.

log.summary: Release 14 lets your vault send and receive photos in messages with your connections.
changes: New: a message can carry one photo (JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to about 8 MB). Your phone sends it to your vault, which keeps a copy for your history and sends a copy to your connection's vault for them.
Your phone never stores photos: it fetches one from your vault when you open it and keeps it only in memory.
Your vault keeps up to 1 GB of photos, sent and received, and accepts at most a quarter of that from any one connection. If a photo cannot be delivered within 7 days, your vault tells you.
Photos travel through VettID's relay encrypted end to end and padded so their size reveals little. Each copy on the relay is deleted once it has been fetched, and after 7 days at the latest.
Sending and viewing photos needs the next app update; until then nothing changes for you.
Built from vettid-vault commit 3dda2b0 (tag release/staging/14) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-16 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Release 15 changes how your vault is recovered and unlocked, so that guesses at your PIN and password are counted where VettID cannot erase them.
changes: New: to recover your vault on a new phone you enter your PIN and credential password together on one screen. You get ten attempts in total for that pair, not ten a day, and a wrong answer never says which of the two was wrong.

After two wrong attempts, each further one waits longer: 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 days, then 30 days. On staging these waits are 10, 20, 40, 80 and 160 minutes. Changing your PIN or password gives you ten new attempts.
Every attempt is counted before it is tested, in a record that is locked for a day on staging (100 years in production). Each one is shown in History and sent to you by email.
A recovery cannot succeed until 72 hours after you last unlocked with both your PIN and password, so someone who starts one while you still use your phone has to wait for you to be absent.
Unlocking now also needs a secret that only your phone's hardware can produce, so your stored vault cannot be used to test PINs without your phone.
A new credential password needs at least 12 characters and must not be a common or easily guessed one.
VettID recovery is on by default for new vaults. Vaults from release 14 or earlier cannot move into release 15 and are set up again.
Needs app version 2.0.0-a1 or later.
Built from vettid-vault commit 2c3fe13 (tag release/staging/15) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-16 with a matching PCR0.
log.security_text: Before release 15, the limits on guessing a PIN and a credential password during a recovery were kept in data that VettID's hosts store, so a host that replayed stored data could have guessed faster than those limits allow. Release 15 keeps the count of attempts where the host cannot remove it and adds a secret from your phone to every unlock. We know of no use of this against any vault.

log.summary: Release 17 lets iPhones running the VettID test app enroll, limits how often a desktop or agent can ask for a session, and fixes wallet and location details.
changes: New: your vault accepts the App Attest data that iOS 27 adds, so an iPhone running the VettID test app can enroll and unlock. Each channel now names its own iOS app.
A desktop or an agent can ask for an access session at most once every 10 minutes, so it cannot flood your phone with prompts.
Wallet: testnet4 is accepted as a network name, a wallet's next addresses move forward when it is updated, and wallets can carry tags like your other items.
Location: you can stop sharing your location even while your daily check is due, and your vault now tells you when a location request is closed.
Release 16 was built but never run; release 17 includes everything it had.
Built from vettid-vault commit 9378113 (tag release/staging/17) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-18 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Release 18 makes staging's waits 24 times shorter for testing, and counts wrong PINs and passwords consistently in credential changes.
changes: Staging only: waits of an hour or more run 24 times faster, so a day is an hour. The daily check comes every hour and a recovery's quiet period is 3 hours. Production is unchanged.
A wrong PIN or password while changing your password, setting up your credential or deleting your vault now counts toward your daily check's limit, as it already did at unlock.
Changing your password, deleting your vault and approving a move check that your phone holds the current credential before they test your PIN, so an outdated copy never uses an attempt.
Built from vettid-vault commit 07bf770 (tag release/staging/18) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-19 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Release 19 runs a newer enclave kernel, lets a recovery count as your daily check, and reports which recovery an unlock on your phone cancelled.
changes: The enclave now runs Linux 6.6.159, the newest 6.6 point release, built by VettID from kernel.org source and reproduced on two builders. It brings three small networking fixes.
Fix: recovering your vault with your PIN and password now counts as your daily check. It restarts the daily check's clock and releases a vault that was held because a check was overdue.

When you stop a recovery by unlocking on your phone, your vault now says which recovery it cancelled, and records it with the unlock as well, so VettID can close that recovery and tell you even if a message is lost.
A request to cancel a recovery can now name the recovery it means, so it never stops a newer one by mistake. VettID's service starts sending the name in a later update.
Built from vettid-vault commit a0b935e (tag release/staging/19) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-19 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Release 20 updates the enclave's certificate checks, marks later recovery attempts urgent again, and finishes a vault deletion that stopped partway.
changes: The enclave and its host are built with Go 1.26.10. Their certificate checks, used for every encrypted connection they make, no longer trust eight intermediate certificates of one certificate authority (CVE-2026-111943).
Fix: after you complete a recovery yourself, a later attempt to recover your vault is marked urgent again. Before, every later attempt in the same round was recorded without urgency.
Fix: a completed recovery now writes its attempts to your History at once, not at your next daily check. A lost confirmation of the successful attempt is sent again when the vault resumes.

When a change of your PIN or password finds recovery attempts it has to close, your vault now records why and tells you with an urgent notice. History also shows the name the recovering phone gave itself.

A vault deletion that stops partway is now finished. The vault asks VettID's host to mark the deletion before it deletes anything, and VettID's cleanup completes a deletion that stopped after that mark.

A one-time key your phone sends is used up as soon as the vault reads the request, even if it refuses it, and your phone can ask the vault to send its set of one-time keys again when they get out of step.

Only one phone holds your credential. Removing a phone clears it, the phone you recover with becomes the only app, and the vault says so when no phone holds it. Copied-vault checks run before a refusal.
The enclave logs a warning when it cannot start a vault's process, and the developer tools refuse to run where vault processes cannot.
Built from vettid-vault commit 577275f (tag release/staging/20) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-20 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Release 21 ends the enclave key a minute early so phones accept it, and adds a History entry when the vault clears a credential holder it cannot find.
changes: The key your phone uses to send requests to the vault now expires 24 hours minus 60 seconds after it is made, not 24 hours. Before, the enclave clock and its attestation clock could differ by a second, and phones then refused every unlock until the key was replaced.

History shows a new entry, "Credential holder cleared", if your vault finds that the phone holding your credential is no longer one of its apps and clears it. Removing a phone already clears it, so this should not happen; if you did not remove a phone, contact VettID.
Built from vettid-vault commit aa4501a (tag release/staging/21) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-22 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Release 22 remembers your vault's Android version of VettID when it moves to an iPhone, so moving back to a different version asks you to confirm.
changes: When your vault moves to an iPhone, it now remembers its Android version of VettID (F-Droid or direct, Google Play, or a development build).

Moving it back to an Android phone with a different version is then a change, as between two Android phones: your old phone is told, your approval names the new version, and History shows "Vault moved to another version of VettID".

Fix: if a recovery had to be resumed after a failed save, the vault forgot which version of VettID it had before, so recovering to a different version was not shown as a change, also between two Android phones.
Built from vettid-vault commit 2550675 (tag release/staging/22) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-24 with a matching PCR0.
log.security_text: Before release 22, if a recovery of your vault had to be resumed because a save on VettID's host failed, the vault forgot which version of VettID it was on before. A recovery to a different version was then not shown as a change: no "Vault moved to another version of VettID" in History and no notice, also between two Android phones. Only a host that failed that one save could cause this. It did not bypass the PIN, the credential password or the recovery code. We know of no use of this against any vault. Vaults on releases 15 to 21 are affected.

log.summary: Release 23 locks a vault whose owner check is overdue, saves its app keys durably, and fixes two recovery edge cases.
changes: A vault whose daily owner check is overdue now locks itself 7 days (by default) after the check was due, and waits for an answered call to end first. A lock your phone sends is tied to the unlock it follows, so a late lock cannot undo a newer unlock.
The vault now saves a new app key only after the host has confirmed the save, and retries a failed save, so a failed save on the host no longer leaves the vault and the phone with different keys.

Fix: repeating a recovery after its second step could leave it stuck; the vault now renews the recovered invitation for the same identity. An unlock that finishes a recovery's last step now also ends the recovery record.
After a transfer, the vault keeps your old phone's pending unlink until it has been delivered. Staging only: support for a staging test certificate is included but switched off.
Built from vettid-vault commit acb007e (tag release/staging/23) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-27 with a matching PCR0.

log.summary: Release 24 makes reconnecting after a restore or a key change more reliable, and lets your phone list requests still waiting.
changes: A connection that could not reconnect after the other side changed its keys now reconnects. Before, every retry was refused and the connection was lost for good.

Reconnecting after a restore, and two people reconnecting at the same moment, now end with one working connection. If a connection shows signs of being restored from an older copy, the vault pauses it and tells you.
If the new keys after a recovery could not be made, the vault now remembers that and tries again at your next unlock, instead of dropping it.
Your phone can now ask the vault for the sign-in, approval and other requests still waiting. They are kept through a lock, a hold or a restart.
Sign-in and approval requests now say what they are for, and the vault keeps the two kinds apart.
Built from vettid-vault commit 214b88f (tag release/staging/24) and independently rebuilt on 2026-10-29 with a matching PCR0.
